content:
alex: ok flagging here — customer acme-app reported a sharp spike of 503s starting ~10:02 UTC. They say requests during multiplexed streaming sessions abruptly fail and they see timeouts in their clients. Logs show upstream worker exits.

maria: got the alert, seeing repeated container restarts on pool gpu-pool-7 around the same time. Kernel messages hint at SIGSEGV in the infer runner.

jamie: Can you paste the worker log snippet? I want to check the stack/addr.

alex: paste: ```
[2026-03-17T10:02:13Z] runner[pid:2345] CRITICAL: coredump: signal 11 (SIGSEGV) at 0x7f2b1a3c
Stack: 0x7f2b1a3c, 0x00000000004f2d, 0x7f2b2d7000
GPU0: GPU OOM before crash? nvml reports exceeded alloc
```

support_tech: customer reports peak concurrent streams ~120 and they were multiplexing small prompt + long toolcall responses. Could be kv-cache blowup + dyn-batching edge.

sre_oncall_bot: INCIDENT: upstream-runner-coredump detected on gpu-pool-7 (auto-created incident 1799123456). Alerting SRE oncall.

maria: trying quick repro on staging with same model + multiplexing, will reproduce memory pattern. If OOM prior to segfault, likely an allocator race when reclaiming KV cache.

jamie: FYI we recently rolled kernel patch that touched memory reclamation for prefetch — linking that here: https://internal/patch/PR-4523. Could be related.

alex: customer ask: "why did this happen during steady QPS?" we should check if bursty concurrent toolcalls cause ephemeral allocation spikes. Also need a timeline for rollback or mitigation.

support_tech: mitigation steps recommended to customer: 1) reduce max_concurrency to 50, 2) disable multiplexing for now, 3) pin to older model variant (v1.3-qr) that has lower KV usage. They implemented reduce concurrency, 503s dropped.

maria: collecting heap profiles, core, and nvml dump. Repro on staging reproduced OOM then segfault after ~30s of sustained multiplexed toolcalls. Attaching minimal repro script in case others want to run: ```python
# repro-multiplex.py
import requests
for i in range(120):
    # open long-poll streaming session with small prompts + toolcall heavy response
    requests.post("https://staging.api.redwood/infer", json={"prompt": "short", "toolcall": True}, timeout=60)
```

jamie: plan: rollback the kernel prefetch change to canary nodes, add temporary guard that caps kv-reserve per-session, and push a hotfix that serializes a portion of the allocator.

alex: escalation to infra: can we get a tactical hotfix window? customer is on Dedicated/hosted and impacted SLA. If we can't hotfix quick, keep guiding them on concurrency cap.

sre_oncall_bot: Pager duty: @sre-team oncall notified.

maria: writing triage notes in the incident board. Next steps: 1) upload core + nvml logs to artifact store 2) run targeted memcheck on allocator 3) run canary rollback and observe 24h 4) coord with support for CS message.

support_tech: CS message drafted: "We observed a regression tied to a recent runtime change that can cause transient GPU memory corruption during high-concurrency multiplexed streaming. We've provided a mitigation (limit concurrency & disable multiplexing) and are rolling a targeted fix. We're prioritizing restoring full capacity while ensuring stability."

jamie: adding repro link + notes to PR. tagging @maria for postmortem lead.

alex: thanks everyone — keeping this thread as the single source. Will update once we have fixation or rollback schedule. :thumbsup:
